questions.prompt: Which of these angles is acute?
questions.explanation: Acute angles are smaller than 90°. 90° is a right angle and 95° is obtuse.

questions.prompt: You bisect an angle of 150°. How big is each part?
questions.explanation: 150 ÷ 2 = 75. Bisect means two equal parts, not three, and not double.

questions.prompt: An angle of 45° is bisected. How big is each part?
questions.explanation: 45 ÷ 2 = 22.5. 90° is double 45°, which is the opposite of bisecting.

questions.prompt: Angles on a straight line add up to...
questions.explanation: A straight line is a half turn, 180°. 360° is for all the angles round a point.

questions.prompt: Four angles meet at a point. Three of them are 90°, 90° and 100°. What is the fourth?
questions.explanation: Angles at a point add up to 360°: 90 + 90 + 100 = 280 and 360 - 280 = 80.

questions.prompt: Two lines cross. One angle is 110°. What is the opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles are equal. 70° is the angle next to it on the straight line.

questions.prompt: A wall meets the floor at 90°. The wall and the floor are...
questions.explanation: Lines or surfaces that meet at 90° are perpendicular. Parallel ones never meet.

questions.prompt: A line crosses two parallel lines. One angle is 48°. What is its alternate angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles (the Z shape) are equal. 132° would be a co-interior angle.

questions.prompt: Two co-interior angles lie between parallel lines. One is 75°. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles add up to 180°: 180 - 75 = 105. Taking 75 from 90 gives 15, which uses the wrong rule.

questions.prompt: A triangle has angles of 80° and 45°. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: 80 + 45 = 125 and 180 - 125 = 55. 125 is only the sum of the two angles you know.
